entities.name: Query Asd protein
observations: 368 aa; calculated molecular weight 39,918 Da and theoretical pI 4.89.
Matches reviewed bacterial aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenases at 66.4–66.7% identity with 99.2–99.7% coverage and E-values of approximately 10^-173 to 10^-174.
Contains Semialdhyde_dh (PF01118) at residues 3–121 and Semialdhyde_dhC (PF02774) at residues 145–353.
Likely cytosolic homodimeric enzyme based on reviewed homolog annotations; exact oligomerization and localization are inferred from homology.
Likely uses NADPH and catalyzes formation of L-aspartate-semialdehyde from L-aspartyl-4-phosphate; EC 1.2.1.11 and Rhea RHEA:24284 are supported by close reviewed homologs.
Participates in the aspartate-family amino-acid biosynthetic branch leading to lysine, methionine, homoserine, and threonine.
Functional assignment is homology-supported rather than directly experimentally established for this exact sequence.

entities.name: Aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase
observations: Reviewed bacterial homologs Q51344, P44801, and P57008 are annotated as NADPH-dependent aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenases.
The enzyme is annotated as a homodimer and cytosolic in representative reviewed homologs.
The catalytic cycle includes an acyl-thioester intermediate and a proton-acceptor catalytic residue in reference proteins.

entities.name: Asd reaction RHEA:24284
observations: L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde + phosphate + NADP(+) = 4-phospho-L-aspartate + NADPH + H(+), represented in the reverse direction of the biosynthetic reaction.
The forward physiological interpretation is reductive dephosphorylation of L-aspartyl-4-phosphate to L-aspartate-semialdehyde using NADPH.

entities.name: Aspartate-family amino acid biosynthesis
observations: Aspartate-semialdehyde is an early branch-point intermediate for de novo lysine, methionine, homoserine, and threonine biosynthesis.
The query protein is inferred to catalyze step 2 of the relevant aspartate-derived pathways.
